name: Cocaine
description: Cocaine facts: medical use as a nasal anesthetic, effects, heart risks, fentanyl contamination, overdose, crack versus powder, treatment, and US penalties.
quick: Cocaine is a stimulant made from the leaves of the coca plant. It has a narrow medical use as a nasal anesthetic, which is why it is Schedule II rather than Schedule I. Illicit cocaine, sold as powder or as smokable crack, is a major cause of heart attacks and overdose deaths, increasingly because it is contaminated with fentanyl.

profile.naloxone: No (but give it if opioids may be involved)

blocks.p: Cocaine blocks the reuptake of dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin, which produces euphoria and stimulation. It also blocks nerve signals, which made it the first local anesthetic. FDA-approved 4% nasal solutions are still used to numb and shrink the lining of the nose before procedures.[[1]][[2]]
Powder cocaine is cocaine hydrochloride, usually snorted. Crack is cocaine processed into a base that can be smoked, reaching the brain faster and more intensely.

sections.q: What are the effects of cocaine, and how long do they last?

blocks.p: Cocaine causes euphoria, energy, talkativeness, alertness, and reduced need for sleep and food, along with a fast heart rate, high blood pressure, dilated pupils, and raised temperature.[[2]]
The high is short: 15 to 30 minutes when snorted and 5 to 10 minutes when smoked. This short duration drives repeated use in binges.

sections.q: What are the risks of cocaine?

blocks.p: **Heart:** cocaine is a leading cause of drug-related heart attacks, even in young people without heart disease. It also causes dangerous heart rhythms, aortic tears, and strokes.[[2]]
**Other harms:** nosebleeds and damage to the nasal septum from snorting, lung damage from smoking crack, seizures, paranoia, and psychosis.
**Levamisole:** a deworming drug often used to cut cocaine can destroy white blood cells and cause skin tissue to die.

blocks.warn: Cocaine is frequently contaminated with fentanyl. People who do not use opioids have no tolerance, and many cocaine-related deaths now involve fentanyl. Test with fentanyl test strips and carry naloxone.

sections.q: What does cocaine overdose look like?

blocks.p: Cocaine overdose can cause chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, very high temperature, severe agitation, seizures, stroke, and sudden collapse. Heart attack can happen even with first-time use.[[2]]

emergency.title: If someone may be overdosing
items: Call 911 for chest pain, a seizure, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke (face drooping, weakness on one side, slurred speech), a very high body temperature, or if the person collapses.
Move them somewhere cool and calm, loosen tight clothing, and cool the skin with water. Do not try to hold them down.
If they become unresponsive or their breathing slows, give naloxone. Street stimulants are often contaminated with fentanyl.
For advice when the person is awake and stable, call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

sections.q: Is cocaine addictive, and what is withdrawal like?

blocks.p: Cocaine is highly addictive. Withdrawal is mainly psychological but can be severe and is a common trigger for relapse.[[2]]

timeline.title: Withdrawal
timeline.text: Low mood, poor concentration, irritability, cravings.

timeline.title: Extinction
timeline.text: Cravings triggered by cues can persist for months.

blocks.p: There is no FDA-approved medicine for cocaine use disorder. Contingency management and cognitive behavioral therapy have the strongest evidence.[[2]]

sections.q: Is cocaine legal in the US?

blocks.p: Cocaine is Schedule II because of its limited medical use as a topical anesthetic, used by clinicians in hospitals and clinics. It is never dispensed to patients to take home.[[3]]

ul: **Possession:** under federal law, a first conviction for possessing any controlled substance without a valid prescription can bring up to one year in prison and a minimum fine of $1,000. Penalties rise with prior convictions.[[4]]

**Trafficking:** trafficking 500 grams or more of cocaine powder, or 28 grams or more of crack, carries a mandatory minimum of 5 years in federal prison. The Fair Sentencing Act of 2010 reduced, but did not eliminate, the gap between crack and powder penalties.[[5]]

**State law:** states set their own penalties, and most drug cases are prosecuted under state law. Penalties range from a civil fine to long prison terms depending on the state, the amount, and prior record.

sections.q: Where can someone get help with cocaine use?

ul: **SAMHSA National Helpline:** 1-800-662-4357. Free, confidential, 24 hours a day, in English and Spanish. It gives referrals to local treatment and support.[[6]]
**FindTreatment.gov:** a federal locator for state-licensed treatment programs, searchable by location, payment, and type of care.[[7]]
**988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline:** call or text 988 for a mental health or substance use crisis.
**Your own clinician:** a primary care doctor can screen, treat, and refer, and can discuss medicines that support recovery where they exist.

faq: Yes, as a 4% nasal solution to numb and shrink the nasal lining before procedures. It is only used by clinicians.
How long does cocaine stay in your system?
Cocaine itself clears in hours, but its metabolite benzoylecgonine is detectable in urine for 2 to 4 days, and longer after heavy use.
Why is cocaine with alcohol dangerous?
The liver combines them into cocaethylene, which lasts longer and is more toxic to the heart.
Can naloxone help in a cocaine overdose?
Naloxone does not reverse cocaine, but give it if the person is unresponsive or breathing poorly, because fentanyl is often present.
What is the difference between crack and cocaine?
Crack is cocaine converted into a smokable base. It reaches the brain faster, producing a shorter, more intense high and a higher risk of addiction.
